competency: Use table elements, attributes, and values in designing web pages
title: Schedule Maker: Web Table Designer
instructions:
Build your class schedule as a table.
1. Add a <table> with a <caption> that says "Grade 12 Class Schedule".
2. Make a header row with <th>: Time, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday.
3. Fill at least 4 rows of time slots with your real subjects.
4. Use colspan or rowspan once, for example, for a recess or lunch break.
5. Add a border and cellpadding so the table is easy to read.
6. Tap Preview, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Use frames in designing web pages
title: Split Screen Web Builder
instructions:
Show two pages on one screen with an iframe.
1. Note: the old <frameset> tag no longer works in modern browsers. We use <iframe> instead.
2. Make a menu with 3 links. Each link has target="viewer".
3. Add an <iframe name="viewer" width="100%" height="300"> under the menu.
4. Use srcdoc on the iframe, or a link to a page that allows embedding, as the starting page.
5. Add a title above the iframe that tells what the learner is looking at.
6. Tap Preview, then Submit.

2. Add a text field for the name, a number field for age, and an email field.
3. Add radio buttons for sex or grade level, and checkboxes for 3 subjects the learner likes.
4. Add a <select> for section and a <textarea> for comments.

subject: dotnet
competency: Perform installation of Integrated Development Environment (IDE) application
title: Tech Ready: IDE Setup Report (laptop)
instructions:
Install an IDE and show proof. Do this on a school laptop.
1. Choose an IDE: Visual Studio Community (with ASP.NET and web development) or Visual Studio Code.
2. Install it. Take screenshots of the download page, the installer, and the finished install.
3. Open the IDE and create a new project or folder. Write a "Hello, World" page or program and run it.
4. Take a screenshot of the code and the output.
5. Write a short Google Doc report: the IDE name and version, the steps you did, one problem you met and how you solved it.
6. Paste all screenshots in the Google Doc and submit the link. Set sharing so your teacher can view it.

5. Make sure the text is easy to read on the background.

Plan a program on paper. Work on a clean sheet.
1. Pick a problem: a grade checker that says Passed or Failed (75 and above passes).
2. Write the algorithm in 5 or fewer numbered steps.
3. Write the pseudocode (START, INPUT, IF, PRINT, END).

subject: dotnet
competency: Apply variables, data types, and functions in creating web applications
title: Function Builder Challenge
instructions:
Write functions that solve a sari-sari store problem.
1. Declare variables with let and const. Use one string, one number, and one boolean.
2. Write a function computeTotal(price, quantity) that returns the total.
3. Write a function computeChange(payment, total) that returns the change.
4. Call both functions and show the results on the page with textContent.
5. Add comments that name each data type you used.
6. Tap Preview, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Use JavaScript operators in problem solving
title: Operator Arena: JS Math Challenge
instructions:
Use operators to solve a canteen problem.
1. Make variables for the price of one item and the quantity.
2. Use arithmetic operators (+, -, *, /, %) to compute total, 10% student discount, and amount to pay.
3. Use comparison operators to check if the payment is enough.
4. Use && or || to check if the learner gets a discount (for example, a student and a total over 100 pesos).
5. Show each result on the page.
6. Tap Preview, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Use event handlers and event listeners in creating web applications

instructions:

when it is clicked. 2. Add an input. Use the "input" event to show what the learner types, live. 3. Add a box that changes color on mouseover and goes back on mouseout. 4. Add one onclick attribute and write a comment on how it differs from addEventListener. 5. Try each action in Preview. 6. Tap Preview, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Use conditional and switch statements in creating web applications
title: Logic Path Explorer: If-Else Adventure
instructions:
Build a grade descriptor checker.
1. Make an input for a grade and a button named Check.
2. On click, read the grade as a number with Number().
3. Use if / else if to show the DepEd descriptor: 90-100 Outstanding, 85-89 Very Satisfactory, 80-84 Satisfactory, 75-79 Fairly Satisfactory, below 75 Did Not Meet Expectations.
4. Show "Invalid grade" for a grade below 0 or above 100.
5. Add a second small program that uses switch to show the day's subject from a number 1 to 5.
6. Tap Preview, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Apply loops in creating a program using while, do while, and for loops
title: Loop Lab: Repeat & Render
instructions:
Use all three loops.
1. Use a for loop to show the multiplication table of 7 from 1 to 10.
2. Use a while loop to count down from 10 to 1.
3. Use a do while loop that adds 5 to a total until the total is more than 30, and show each total.
4. Show each result in a <ul> by creating <li> items.
5. Add a comment that tells when you would pick each loop.
6. Tap Preview, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Use JavaScript arrays in creating a program
title: Smart List Builder: Array in Action
instructions:
Manage a list with an array.
1. Make an array of 5 subjects.
2. Use push to add one, pop to remove the last, and unshift or shift for the first.
3. Use a for loop and forEach to show every item in a list.
4. Use indexOf or includes to check if "Mathematics" is in the list.
5. Show the array length and the final list on the page.
6. Tap Preview, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Create objects to display the set of properties and values
title: Object Explorer: My Digital Profile
instructions:
Build a digital profile object.
1. Make an object named me with name, age, grade, section, and a hobbies array.
2. Add one method to the object, for example, introduce(), that returns a sentence.
3. Show every key and value on the page using a for...in loop.
4. Add a new property after the object is made, and change one value.
5. Show the result of me.introduce().
6. Tap Preview, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Apply Document Object Model (DOM) nodes in creating a web document
title: DOM Master: Control the Web Page
instructions:
Control a page with the DOM.
1. Add an input, an Add button, and an empty <ul id="todo">.
2. On click, create an <li> with createElement and add the typed text with textContent.
3. Add the item to the list with appendChild.
4. Add a Remove button inside each item that deletes it with remove().
5. Use querySelector to change the page title text when the list has 5 items.
6. Tap Preview, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Discuss the C# fundamentals
title: Build Your First C# App
instructions:
Write your first C# program.
1. Keep the Program class and the Main method.
2. Print a welcome line with Console.WriteLine.
3. Ask for the learner's name with Console.Write and read it with Console.ReadLine().
4. Print "Hello, " followed by the name, and the learner's school.
5. Write one comment that says what Main does.
6. Type your input in Program input, tap Run, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Use C# data types, variables, strings, and constants in creating a web application
title: Data Detective: C# Variables
instructions:
Make a sari-sari store receipt.
1. Declare a string for the item name, an int for the quantity, and a double for the price.
2. Declare a const for the discount rate (for example, 0.05).
3. Read the item name, quantity, and price with Console.ReadLine() and convert the numbers with int.Parse and double.Parse.
4. Compute the total and the discount. Print the receipt with string interpolation, for example $"Total: {total:F2}".
5. Type three input lines (name, quantity, price) in Program input.
6. Type your input in Program input, tap Run, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Apply C# operators and decision making in problem solving
title: Decision Engine: C# Logic Builder
instructions:
Write a grade checker.
1. Read a grade (0-100) with Console.ReadLine() and convert it with int.Parse.
2. Use if / else if to print: 90-100 Outstanding, 85-89 Very Satisfactory, 80-84 Satisfactory, 75-79 Fairly Satisfactory, below 75 Did Not Meet Expectations.
3. Print "Invalid grade" if it is below 0 or above 100 (use || ).
4. Type a grade in Program input, tap Run, try at least 3 different grades, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Use the C# iteration statements in creating a web application
title: Iteration Challenge: Smart Counter
instructions:
Build a smart counter.
1. Read a number n from Program input.
2. Use a for loop to print the numbers from 1 to n.
3. Use a while loop to compute the sum of the numbers from 1 to n.
4. Use foreach on a string array of 3 school subjects and print each one.
5. Print the even numbers from 1 to n using a loop and the % operator.
6. Type your input in Program input, tap Run, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Apply C# classes, methods and structure in creating a web application
title: Class Creator: My First C# Blueprint
instructions:
Make a Student class.
1. Write a class named Student with fields for name, grade level, and section.
2. Add a method Introduce() that prints a sentence with those values.
3. Add a constructor that sets the three fields.
4. In Main, create 2 Student objects with different values and call Introduce() on each.
5. Tap Run, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Create web application programs that contains C# arrays
title: Smart Array System
instructions:
Process a list of grades with an array.
1. Declare an int array of 5 grades. Fill it with 5 lines of input using a for loop.
2. Compute and print the average, the highest, and the lowest grade.
3. Count how many grades are 75 or above and print the number of passed.
4. Type 5 grades on 5 lines in Program input.
5. Type your input in Program input, tap Run, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Apply the C# Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) approach in creating a web application
title: OOP Builder: School System
instructions:
Model a school system with OOP.
1. Write a base class Person with Name and a virtual method Describe().
2. Write Student and Teacher classes that inherit from Person. Student has a grade level and Teacher has a subject.
3. Override Describe() in each class so it prints the right sentence.
4. Use private fields with public properties (encapsulation) for at least one class.
5. In Main, put 3 objects in a Person array and call Describe() in a loop.
6. Tap Run, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Utilize the C# file input/output in creating, deleting, and reading web applications
title: File Flow: Save & Retrieve
instructions:
Save and read a file.
1. Use File.WriteAllText to save 3 lines (for example, learner names) to a file named list.txt.
2. Use File.Exists to check the file, then File.ReadAllText or File.ReadAllLines to read it and print the lines.
3. Use File.AppendAllText to add one more line, then read and print again.
4. Use File.Delete to remove the file and print whether it still exists.
5. Add a using System.IO; line at the top.
6. Tap Run, then Submit.

subject: dotnet
competency: Discuss the ASP.NET Model View Controller (MVC) fundamentals
title: MVC Explorer: Blueprint Diagram
instructions:
Draw the MVC blueprint. Use paper or a printed sheet.
1. Draw three boxes: Model, View, Controller.
2. Use one school example: a page that shows a student's grades.
3. Under each box, write what it does and the name of the C# file or class it would be.
4. Draw arrows for how the three talk to each other, and label each arrow.
5. Write 2 sentences at the bottom: why MVC is easier to manage than putting everything in one file.
6. Take one clear photo of the diagram and submit it.

subject: dotnet
competency: Discuss the ASP.NET MVC environment and life cycle
title: Life Cycle Simulator: Request to Response
instructions:
Draw the life cycle of one request, from browser to response. Use paper.
1. Use this example: a learner opens /Students/Index.
2. Draw the steps in order: browser request, routing, controller and action, model and data, view, response in the browser.
3. Write the name of the file or class at each step.
4. Add a note where a filter or middleware could run.
5. Take one clear photo of the diagram and submit it.

subject: dotnet
competency: Perform configurations of the routing process in directing an http request in an ASP.NET MVC project using controllers and actions
title: Route Finder: Controllers and Actions
instructions:
Set up routing in an ASP.NET MVC project. Do this on a school laptop.
1. Create an ASP.NET MVC project named SchoolRoutes.
2. Make a StudentsController with 3 actions: Index, Details(int id), and Search(string name).
3. Set the default route in the route config. Add one custom route, for example, /grades/{section}/{id}.
4. Make a simple view for each action so the pages show text, and test each URL in the browser.
5. Submit: (a) your GitHub repo or Drive folder link, (b) a link to a 1-3 minute screen recording that shows the project working, (c) screenshots of the main pages, saved in the same folder.

subject: dotnet
competency: Use filters, selectors, and views in creating projects
title: View Master: Filter & Display
instructions:
Use filters and views in an ASP.NET MVC project. Do this on a school laptop.
1. Create a project named LearnerList. Make a model Learner (Name, GradeLevel, Section).
2. Make a LearnersController that sends a list of 8 learners to a view.
3. Show the list in a table with a Razor foreach. Add a search box and a grade-level filter that uses a query string.
4. Add one action filter, for example, [Authorize] or a custom logging filter, and write what it does in a comment.
5. Submit: (a) your GitHub repo or Drive folder link, (b) a link to a 1-3 minute screen recording that shows the project working, (c) screenshots of the main pages, saved in the same folder.

subject: dotnet
competency: Apply the ASP.NET MVC - data model

Build a model for student records. Do this on a school laptop.

2. Make a Student model with Id, FullName, GradeLevel, Section, and GeneralAverage.
3. Make a controller that holds a list of at least 5 students and a view that shows them in a table.
4. Add a Details page for one student.
5. Submit: (a) your GitHub repo or Drive folder link, (b) a link to a 1-3 minute screen recording that shows the project working, (c) screenshots of the main pages, saved in the same folder.

subject: dotnet

Use HTML helpers to make a form. Do this on a school laptop.

2. Make a Create page that uses Html.BeginForm, Html.LabelFor, Html.TextBoxFor, Html.DropDownListFor, Html.CheckBoxFor, and Html.TextAreaFor.
3. Add a submit button and show the saved values on a confirmation page.
4. Submit: (a) your GitHub repo or Drive folder link, (b) a link to a 1-3 minute screen recording that shows the project working, (c) screenshots of the main pages, saved in the same folder.

2. Make an Enrollment model (Name, Strand, GradeLevel).
3. Make a form that posts to an action. Show the model values on the next page.
4. Make a second action that takes values from the query string and from the route, to compare the ways of binding.
5. Submit: (a) your GitHub repo or Drive folder link, (b) a link to a 1-3 minute screen recording that shows the project working, (c) screenshots of the main pages, saved in the same folder.

instructions:

2. Make a Learner model and add Required, StringLength, and Range validation attributes.
